symptom: PUT /snapshot/load fails with CRC validation error. Snapshot state file is corrupted (interrupted write, disk corruption, transport error).

diagnostic_steps.action: Verify state file size and basic readability
Compute external checksum to compare with the source
diagnostic_steps.expected: Matches the checksum recorded at snapshot-create time (orchestrator's responsibility)

fix_steps.action: Restore from a backup snapshot (orchestrator-managed retention)
fix_steps.command: Pick last-known-good snap.bin + snap.mem from backup

fix_steps.action: Implement mandatory checksum verification in snapshot transport
fix_steps.command: Add SHA256 + signature alongside snap.bin/snap.mem in your storage tier

symptom: Snapshot restore on cgroup-v1 hosts is significantly slower than v2 — restore times of 100ms+ vs 5-15ms on v2.

fix_steps.action: Migrate host to cgroup v2 (kernel 5.10+ default on most distros)
fix_steps.command: Add systemd.unified_cgroup_hierarchy=1 to host kernel cmdline; reboot

symptom: ARM snapshot restore fails when GIC version differs between save host (e.g., GICv2) and restore host (e.g., GICv3). Device-state mismatch.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check GIC version on both hosts
diagnostic_steps.expected: Should show 'GICv2' or 'GICv3' line — must match

fix_steps.action: Restrict snapshot fleet to a single GIC version
fix_steps.command: Tag/group hosts by GIC version in your scheduler

symptom: After snapshot restore, MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL value differs from pre-snapshot. Workload that overwrote this MSR sees the host default after restore. Only happens when no CPU template is in use.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check guest MSR pre and post restore

fix_steps.action: Apply a CPU template that includes MSR_IA32_TSX_CTRL
fix_steps.command: Use static template (T2/T2S) or PUT /cpu-config with custom template containing the MSR

symptom: Snapshot restore fails (or guest time runs at wrong rate) when source and destination hosts have different TSC frequencies and KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL is unavailable.

diagnostic_steps.command: Check kernel version + try a minimal KVM_SET_TSC_KHZ ioctl

fix_steps.action: Restrict snapshot fleet to homogeneous TSC frequency hosts
fix_steps.command: Tag/group hosts by TSC freq in scheduler

fix_steps.action: Upgrade restore host kernel to one with KVM_CAP_TSC_CONTROL
fix_steps.command: Standard kernel update

symptom: Snapshot restore fails because CPUID exposed at save time references features unavailable on the restore host (e.g., AVX-512 absent on target).

diagnostic_steps.expected: Save host has features missing on restore host

fix_steps.action: Use a CPU template that targets the LCD across the fleet (e.g., T2 for Intel-broad)
fix_steps.command: PUT /cpu-config with a portable template before save; re-save
fix_steps.rollback: Use no template (lock fleet to identical CPUs)

symptom: virtio-block VIRTIO_BLK_T_FLUSH command issued by guest doesn't reach the host kernel block layer. Risk of data loss on host crash even though guest believes data is durable.

diagnostic_steps.expected: cache_type='Unsafe' explicitly drops flushes; 'Writeback' should propagate

diagnostic_steps.action: Trace block layer to confirm FLUSH propagation
diagnostic_steps.command: host$ sudo bpftrace -e 'tracepoint:block:block_rq_issue { if (str(args->comm) == "firecracker") { printf("%s", args->cmd); } }'

fix_steps.action: Set drive cache_type to Writeback (NOT Unsafe)
fix_steps.command: PUT /drives/<id> {cache_type: 'Writeback', ...}

fix_steps.action: Track upstream issue #2172 for any additional fixes; upgrade Firecracker when available
fix_steps.command: Monitor github.com/firecracker-microvm/firecracker/issues/2172

symptom: Restoring a snapshot taken during early guest kernel boot causes the resumed guest to crash. VMGenID device wasn't fully initialized when snapshot was taken.

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify when the original snapshot was taken
diagnostic_steps.command: Check orchestrator logs for snapshot-create timestamp relative to InstanceStart
diagnostic_steps.expected: Snapshot taken before guest finished booting userspace

fix_steps.action: Take snapshots only AFTER guest has fully booted (init system ready, /var/run/sysinit-progress complete)
fix_steps.command: Orchestrator waits for guest readiness signal (vsock ping / SSH / cloud-init done) before pause+snapshot

symptom: PUT /snapshot/create with snapshot_type=Diff returns 400. machine-config.track_dirty_pages was not set to true at boot, so KVM has no dirty bitmap to query.

diagnostic_steps.expected: Should be true for diff snapshots; if false → root cause

fix_steps.action: Enable track_dirty_pages BEFORE InstanceStart (it's pre-boot only)
fix_steps.command: PUT /machine-config {vcpu_count: ..., mem_size_mib: ..., track_dirty_pages: true}
fix_steps.rollback: Drop diff snapshots; use Full only

fix_steps.action: If VM is already running, take a Full snapshot, restore with enable_diff_snapshots=true (re-enables tracking on the restored VM)
fix_steps.command: PUT /snapshot/create {snapshot_type: 'Full', ...}; PUT /snapshot/load {..., enable_diff_snapshots: true}
fix_steps.validation: Subsequent diff snapshots work on the restored VM

symptom: Guest crashes mysteriously after restore — page faults can't be served. The MAP_PRIVATE-backed memory file was deleted from the host while the resumed VM was still running.

diagnostic_steps.action: Check if mem file still exists

diagnostic_steps.expected: Mapping present and points at a deleted file (shown with '(deleted)')

fix_steps.action: Mark the mem file immutable for VM lifetime in your orchestrator
fix_steps.command: Track per-VM dependency: don't delete mem file until VM process exits
fix_steps.validation: Long-running restored VMs no longer crash on cold pages

fix_steps.action: Use Uffd backend instead — orchestrator-supplied page handler decouples mem file lifetime
fix_steps.command: PUT /snapshot/load with mem_backend.backend_type='Uffd'
fix_steps.validation: Mem file can be retired earlier (or not stored as a file at all)
fix_steps.rollback: Revert to File backend; reinstate file-pinning policy

symptom: Restored VM hangs on cold-page access. The userfaultfd handler process crashed or blocked, so page faults from KVM never get serviced.

diagnostic_steps.expected: vCPU thread blocked in KVM_RUN waiting for page fault completion

fix_steps.action: Restart the UFFD handler with fault-tolerance — it should re-attach to existing FCs via the per-VM UDS
fix_steps.command: Implement: handler process registers with new VMs but also re-binds to existing UDSes on restart
fix_steps.validation: Handler restart doesn't kill running VMs

fix_steps.action: If unrecoverable, kill the FC process and restart from snapshot
fix_steps.command: kill -9 <fc-pid>; orchestrator restarts new FC + new UFFD handler
fix_steps.validation: New VM boots; old session lost

symptom: After snapshot restore, in-flight TCP connections to the guest break. ARP cache is stale, switches haven't seen the new MAC's frames yet.
error_patterns: no route to host after restore

diagnostic_steps.action: Confirm network state is the issue
diagnostic_steps.command: guest$ ip a; ip route; arp -a
diagnostic_steps.expected: Routes present; but external peer ARP cache may be stale

fix_steps.action: Send gratuitous ARPs from the guest immediately on resume
fix_steps.command: guest$ arping -c 3 -A -I eth0 <guest-ip> (in init script)
fix_steps.validation: Switch ARP tables refresh; peers can reach guest

fix_steps.action: For multi-clone deployments, give each clone a unique TAP and unique guest IP
fix_steps.command: Per-clone setup: ip netns + ip tuntap add + per-clone NAT rules

fix_steps.action: Design app protocols to be reconnect-tolerant
fix_steps.command: Application-level: idempotent operations + auto-reconnect logic
fix_steps.validation: Resume disruptions are invisible to end users
